focus: General counter 개 takes native numbers (다섯 개) – near-dup group of 2, re-anchor distinctly in the drama-seasons context.
된 after a duration noun means 'that has lasted X' (십 년 된 친구 = a friendship of ten years) – add romanization for the quoted chunk.
Long negation -지 않다 and short 안 are interchangeable (많지 않아요 = 안 많아요) – fix em dash and romanize both forms.
못 before a verb = 'can't' (vs 안 = 'don't') – romanize the card's 못 사귀어요.
-아/어서 marks cause ('because') – romanize the card's 비슷해서.
-아/어 주다 = do something as a favor for someone – romanize the card's 지켜 줬어요.
-든지 builds any-words (뭐든지 anything, 누구든지 anyone) – reusable series; fix em dash and romanize the example.
수다를 떨다 literally uses 떨다 (shake/rattle) – give the literal image instead of a bare gloss; fix em dash.
말이 통하다 literally 'words pass through' (통하다 = flow/get through) – surface the literal logic behind 'clicking'.
첫눈에 반하다 = fall 'at first eye' – give the literal breakdown of 첫눈에 with romanization.
-기 turns the verb into a noun so 시작하다 can attach (사귀기 시작했어요) – romanize the example.
좋아하다 is already a verb, so 3rd-person 좋아해요 needs no -어하다, unlike feeling adjectives – romanize the cited forms.
긴장되다 uses 되다 = 'become': nerves happen to you rather than being something you are – rebuild on that insight, fix em dash.
통화하다 = have a phone conversation vs 전화하다 = place a call – romanize both members of the pair.
생각이 나다: the thought is the subject that 'arises' on its own – keep this one rule, drop the 자꾸 gloss, romanize.
-지 못하다 is the long form of 못 'can't' – romanize the card's 고백하지 못했어요.
-(으)면 covers both 'if' and 'when' – English splits the two, Korean doesn't; romanize the card's 사귀면.
-보다 = 'than' attaches directly to the compared noun (연애보다) – romanize the example.
-고 chains verbs and only the last one carries the tense (잡고 걸었어요) – romanize the example.
께서 is the honorific subject marker and pairs with -시- on the verb – romanize the card's 나셨어요.
께 replaces 한테/에게 when the receiver is honored (부모님께) – near-dup group of 3, re-anchor distinctly to this card.
-(으)ㄹ게요 is a promise to the listener, not a plain future – romanize the card's 사과할게요.
다시는 + -지 않을게요 = a 'never again' promise – distinct negative-promise angle; add romanization throughout.
주다 becomes 주시다 to honor the person doing the favor (이해해 주셨어요) – romanize the example.
-어하다 is only for inner feelings; appearance adjectives like 아름답다 stay plain even for others – add romanization.
In guesses the tense sits on 같다: 같았어요 makes it a guess about the past – romanize the example.
-시길 바라요 puts the honor on the person being wished well – romanize the card's 행복하시길 바라요.
Verb + -는 sits in front of a noun like an adjective (좋아하는 가수) – English's relative clause reversed; fix em dash.
-만에 = 'in only that much time' (십 분 만에) – keep this one rule, drop the 매진되다 gloss, romanize.
-자마자 = 'as soon as', zero gap between the two events – romanize the card's 나오자마자.
과 after consonants, 와 after vowels (춤과 노래) – keep the and-particle rule, drop the 둘 다 gloss, romanize.
-이나 adds surprise at the amount: 세 곡이나 = 'three whole songs' – romanize the example.
여운 is literally a lingering echo that 남다 (remains) – the concert keeps ringing; build the tip on that image.
-부터 marks the starting point; 때부터 = 'since the time of' (데뷔 때부터) – romanize the example.
-자고 하다 reports a 'let's' suggestion (가자고 했어요) – romanize the example.
Location words are nouns: 무대 위의 = 'the stage's top' linked with 의 – keep that single rule and romanize.
-방 (room) builds venue words: 노래방 = song-room, same pattern as PC방 – reusable compound logic, romanize.
Noun + 를 위해 = 'for the sake of' (가수를 위해) – romanize the example.
-(으)러 가다 = go somewhere in order to do something (보러 갔어요) – romanize the example.
N을 바탕으로 = 'with N as the base/foundation' (실화를 바탕으로) – romanize the example.
인기가 많다 literally 'popularity is plentiful' – in Korean you have much popularity rather than being popular; keep that single rule.
-아/어서 sequencing: the second action uses the first's result (사서 먹었어요 = bought it and ate that popcorn), unlike plain -고 – romanize.
몰다 = to herd/drive together: 몰아서 보다 = herding episodes into one sitting – give the literal image, romanize.
-적인 turns Sino nouns into adjectives: 감동 (emotion) becomes 감동적인 (moving) – reusable suffix, romanize.
